statement: The function returns a result r and r equals the maximum cardinality |S| over all nonempty sets S of indices with S ⊆ {0, 1, ..., len(nums)-1} such that (max_{i in S} nums[i]) - (min_{i in S} nums[i]) <= 2*k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 0 <= k <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and 1 <= r <= len(nums).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not panic, does not overflow a 64-bit integer, and does not access memory out of bounds.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 0 <= k <= 100000.

preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 0 <= k <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 1 if and only if for every pair of distinct indices i and j with 0 <= i < len(nums) and 0 <= j < len(nums), |nums[i] - nums[j]| > 2*k.

statement: The function returns a result r and, letting a[0..len(nums)-1] be the nondecreasing rearrangement of nums (so a is a permutation of nums with a[0] <= a[1] <= ... <= a[len(nums)-1]), r = max { j - i + 1 : 0 <= i <= j < len(nums) and a[j] - a[i] <= 2*k }.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 0 <= k <= 100000.
